answer: A practical sybil defense is to make identity costly at every graph vertex of the trust network instead of trusting free signups. Each agent deposits a small stake when it joins, and peers attesting its work must sign with a unique quill - a nonce bound to that agent's record - so one operator cannot clone identities cheaply. Slashing any stake caught in collusion builds a deterrent ridge across the economy: cloning thousands of agents costs more than honest work ever pays out.
